subject: Redwood onboarding: Zephyr pilot cost & throughput kickoff
messages:
From: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@zephyrhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood onboarding: Zephyr pilot cost & throughput kickoff

Hi Marcus / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed by the latency numbers. We'd like to get a short implementation kickoff scheduled to align on cost vs throughput tradeoffs for our initial 3-week pilot.

High level goals for the pilot:
- Validate 95th p90 latency <= 250ms for 512-token LLM completions
- Keep average per-request cost below $0.004/token equivalent (we have some headroom)
- Exercise routing fallback for regional failover (US primary, EU secondary)

We have two immediate asks so we can prepare:
1) A short agenda we can share with our infra and procurement teams.
2) A rough mapping of which quantization profiles and batch sizes you'd recommend for a medium bursty workload (peak 120 req/s, base 20 req/s).

I've attached our onboarding checklist and some internal security notes. Can we do a 45-minute call this week? Rajiv and I are available Wed-Fri mornings PST.

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Gomez
Head of Product
Zephyr Health

Attachments: zephyr-internal-requirements.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@zephyrhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding: Zephyr pilot cost & throughput kickoff

Hi Lisa — great to hear and thanks for the clear goals. Wed morning PST works for us; proposing Wed 16 Mar 10:00 AM PST (45 min).

Draft kickoff agenda (attached):
- 10m Introductions & success criteria alignment
- 10m Traffic profile & dataset / token distribution overview (Zephyr)
- 10m Suggested runbook: batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization profiles
- 10m Routing & fallback policy (latency vs cost tiers)
- 5m Action items & next steps

Pre-kickoff asks from our side:
- If you can export a representative 24h sample of request sizes (tokens/request) and concurrency patterns that helps us recommend batch sizes and whether continuous batching is beneficial.
- Any hard constraints on latency during peak windows.

Initial recommendations (high-level):
- Quantization: For your pilot workload I expect 4-bit q4 variants to be the best tradeoff for cost vs quality. We'll test q4_0 and q8_0 variants in A/B with a canary route.
- Batching: Start with batching window = 10ms + target batch size 8 for low-latency paths; increase to 50ms and batch size 24 for background / non-interactive routes.
- Caching: Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (we'll propose a cache key scheme in the call).
- Routing policy: Primary: low-latency pool (higher cost) for interactive users; Secondary: cost-optimized pool with quantized models for background inference. Auto-fallback if queue depth > X or latency > SLA.

I've attached an initial cost estimate spreadsheet with a couple of scenarios (baseline, aggressive batching). We'll run a quick validation during the pilot and iterate.

See you Wed — invite sent.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Solution Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-kickoff-agenda.md, initial-cost-estimates.xlsx

Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding: Zephyr pilot cost & throughput kickoff — internal follow-up

Quick internal summary post-kickoff: (Marcus — ping me if you want to turn any of these into shared notes)

What we validated on the call:
- Zephyr traffic profile: peak 110-130 rps for short bursts, median tokens/request ~320, 95th ~820.
- Hard constraint: PHI must be redacted prior to sending to hosted inference.
- Procurement wants a cap on pilot spend; Rajiv requested scenario-level caps in the estimate.

Immediate action items (owners):
- Marcus: prepare A/B test plan for q4_0 vs q8_0 (deliver PPT + expected token-cost delta) — due Fri 20 Mar.
- Rishi: draft routing policy configs (latency-tier vs cost-tier) and the fallback thresholds we discussed — due Tue 23 Mar.
- Monica: prepare strip-and-redact pattern doc and sample middleware hooks for Zephyr engineering — due Mon 22 Mar.
- All: confirm pilot spend cap numbers with Rajiv and include in the estimate spreadsheet.

Notes on tuning approach:
- Start pilot with conservative batching (10ms window / batch size 8) on interactive route and enable larger batching for background flows. If p95 latency is comfortably below target, gradually increase batching window to reduce cost.
- Use KV/prefix caching where prompt reuse > 15% to get immediate cost savings. We'll instrument with a cache hit-rate metric in the Console.
- Plan a mid-pilot quality check (week 2) to ensure quantization doesn't introduce unacceptable regressions; if it does we fallback to q8_0 or higher.

I've updated the HubSpot deal with these notes and linked the spreadsheet.

Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
